podcast.body: "Higher Ground" was composed and recorded by Stevie Wonder utilizing the TONTO synthesizer. This track, like many others from his 1970s output, was a result of his collaboration with Malcolm Cecil and Robert Margouleff, showcasing the groundbreaking electronic textures they achieved. "Just like superstition, living for the city, boogie on reggae woman, higher ground, and many others were all composed and recorded using Tonto."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Unsung Heroes of Music: Part 1

podcast.body: Stevie Wonder is the original songwriter of "Higher Ground." When the Red Hot Chili Peppers' cover of this song became a hit on US radio, he received all the money from its airplay in the United States, as the US system pays only songwriters and publishers for radio play. "It was the songwriter. Stevie Wonder, he got all the money."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Stevie Wonder's classic song was given a "scorching cover" by the Red Hot Chili Peppers on their 1989 album "Mother's Milk," helping them solidify their claim on the emerging alt-rock scene. "scorching cover of a Stevie Wonder class."
